  2: name: Per-Turn Enforcement Protocol
  3: description: Required workflow for every user message in a Codex session. Opens a session log turn, logs all code edits, verifies builds, and closes the turn before responding. Use EVERY user message — this is not optional.
  4: ---
  5: 
  6: ## Overview
  7: 
  8: Codex CLI lacks a hook system, so the Per-User-Message protocol from
  9: `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` must be invoked manually. This skill wraps that
 10: protocol in three scripts located in the plugin's `lib/` directory.
 11: 
 12: Run `PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/session-start.ps1 <workspace-path>` once per
 13: workspace before Phase 1, or let `user-prompt-submit.ps1` auto-bootstrap the
 14: session cache on first use. Runtime state is scoped under
 15: `cache/workspaces/<workspace-key>/sessions/<session-key>/`.
 16: 
 17: **Every user message MUST flow through these three phases.** If you skip any
 18: phase your session log is incomplete and the workspace's AGENTS-README-FIRST
 19: contract is violated.
 20: 
 21: ## Phase 1 — Open a Turn (before any tool call)
 22: 
 23: Invoke on every new user prompt **before** calling any other tool:
 24: 
 25: ```powershell
 26: echo '{"prompt":"<verbatim user message>"}' | PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/user-prompt-submit.ps1
 27: ```
 28: 
 29: The script:
 30: - Auto-bootstraps scoped `session-state.yaml` when the marker file is trusted
 31: - Reads scoped `session-state.yaml` for the active `sessionId`
 32: - Builds a fresh `requestId` of the form `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-prompt-xxxx`
 33: - Calls `workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn` with the prompt as `queryText`
 34: - Writes scoped `current-turn.yaml` with `turnRequestId`, `codeEdits: 0`,
 35:   `lastBuildStatus: unknown`, `status: in_progress`
 36: - Emits a reminder via `additionalContext` that Phases 2 and 3 are mandatory
 37: 
 38: If the script outputs `status: no-session`, do not treat that as a final best-effort state. The hook has already health-checked the marker, attempts session creation when the marker timestamp changes, submits triage if creation fails after a healthy bootstrap, and records degraded recovery state under the failsafe path. Continue the user request, but preserve the `recoveryStatus`, `healthStatus`, and `failsafePath` receipt as evidence; retry session creation only after `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` is rewritten or the hook reports recovery.
 39: 
 40: ## Phase 2 — After Every Code Edit
 41: 
 42: Immediately after you write or edit any source file
 43: (`.cs`, `.axaml`, `.xaml`, `.csproj`, `.fsproj`, `.vbproj`, `.razor`,
 44: `.cshtml`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`) invoke:
 45: 
 46: ```powershell
 47: echo '{"tool_name":"Edit","tool_input":{"file_path":"<absolute path>"}}' \
 48:   | PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/code-verify.ps1
 49: ```
 50: 
 51: The script:
 52: - Locates the nearest project file (`.csproj` / `package.json`)
 53: - Runs the matching build command (`dotnet build` or `tsc --noEmit`)
 54: - Parses the output and writes the status (`succeeded` / `failed`) to
 55:   scoped `current-turn.yaml` under `lastBuildStatus`
 56: - Records the code edit count via `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`
 57: - Appends a `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions` entry
 58: - If the build failed, its stdout contains the first 10 errors; those
 59:   errors are the reason you must fix the build before Phase 3
 60: 
 61: **Do not move on to the next edit or close the turn while
 62: `lastBuildStatus: failed` is cached.** Fix the errors first.
 63: 
 64: ## Phase 3 — Close the Turn (before your final response)
 65: 
 66: Before emitting your response to the user, invoke:
 67: 
 68: ```powershell
 69: PowerShell ${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/lib/stop-gate.ps1
 70: ```
 71: 
 72: The script checks scoped `current-turn.yaml` and returns `decision: block`
 73: with a reason in any of these cases:
 74: - `status: in_progress` — you forgot to call `workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn`
 75: - `codeEdits > 0 && lastBuildStatus = failed` — build is broken
 76: 
 77: When blocked, finish the missing step:
 78: 
 79: ```yaml
 80: # Complete the turn
 81: type: request
 82: payload:
 83:   requestId: req-<new-id>
 84:   method: workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn
 85:   params:
 86:     response: |
 87:       <one-paragraph summary of what was delivered>
 88: ```
 89: 
 90: Then re-run `stop-gate.ps1`. Repeat until it returns `status: passed`.
 91: 
 92: If the build is intentionally left broken (rare), touch
 93: scoped `turn-accept-failure.marker` *before* the next `stop-gate.ps1` call;
 94: the script consumes the marker on its next pass.
 95: 
 96: ## Contract
 97: 
 98: This protocol exists because:
 99: - `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` Rule 2 requires a session log turn per user message
100: - `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` Rule 10 requires you to verify code compiles
101: - `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` "Before Delivering Output" requires the session
102:   log to be current before you respond
103: 
104: Skipping any phase leaves the contract broken. If you forget mid-turn,
105: invoke the missing phase as soon as you notice; partial compliance beats none.
106: 
107: ## Integration With Your Workflow
108: 
109: The three scripts are idempotent for the lifetime of one turn. They read
110: and update the current session's scoped `current-turn.yaml` which is created
111: in Phase 1 and consumed by Phase 3. The scoped cache is the source of truth
112: for turn state — never infer turn status from memory or conversation.
113:

117: - `skills/todo/SKILL.md` — TODO management
118: - `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` (workspace root) — authoritative contract

  1: ---
  2: name: TODO Management
  3: description: Use when the user asks to "create a todo", "list todos", "update todo", "query tasks", "check todo status", "plan implementation", or "mark todo done".
  4: version: 0.1.0
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: # TODO Management
  8: 
  9: ## Overview
 10: 
 11: To interact with project TODOs, use the `workflow.todo.*` REPL command namespace through `lib/repl-invoke.ps1` via the `PowerShell.MCP wrapper`. The wrapper accepts the documented params, validates them, and sends a single-line JSON request envelope to `PowerShell.MCP wrapper`. Direct stdio callers must use the same shape: one single-line JSON request envelope per message, not formatted YAML. The server returns a `type: result` or `type: error` envelope on stdout. Streaming commands additionally emit a sequence of `type: event` envelopes before the final result.
 12: 
 13: The YAML blocks in this skill illustrate the logical structure of each envelope for readability; the actual wire format is single-line JSON.
 14: 
 15: ## Session Log Bootstrap
 16: 
 17: Before using any workflow commands, call `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` to initialize the session log subsystem:
 18: 
 19: ```yaml
 20: type: request
 21: payload:
 22:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
 23:   method: workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap
 24:   params: {}
 25: ```
 26: 
 27: This call is idempotent and should be made once per conversation context.
 28: 
 29: ## Usage Guidance
 30: 
 31: Use TODO data to refine or confirm the current plan after checking session/task state. Do not start with TODO enumeration when session state already identifies the active task.
 32: 
 33: ## Internal TODO Tracking Toggle
 34: 
 35: By default, the agent keeps transient checklist state locally and uses MCP TODOs only when the task needs durable workspace TODO tracking. To make MCP TODOs the backing store for durable plan items in a workspace:
 36: 
 37: ```yaml
 38: type: request
 39: payload:
 40:   requestId: req-20260409T115900Z-todo-internal-enable
 41:   method: workflow.todo.internal.enable
 42:   params: {}
 43: ```
 44: 
 45: To turn it off:
 46: 
 47: ```yaml
 48: type: request
 49: payload:
 50:   requestId: req-20260409T115901Z-todo-internal-disable
 51:   method: workflow.todo.internal.disable
 52:   params: {}
 53: ```
 54: 
 55: `workflow.todo.internal.status` reports the active state and whether it came from the cached setting, default behavior, or an environment override. An environment-variable override, when set, takes precedence over the cached setting for the current process: set it to `1` to force-enable internal tracking or `0` to force-disable it. The plugin defines the specific override variable name.
 56: 
 57: ## TODO ID Naming Conventions
 58: 
 59: Persist only IDs that conform to one of two patterns:
 60: 
 61: - `^[A-Z]+-[A-Z0-9]+-\d{3}$`: three-segment uppercase kebab-case, e.g. `PLAN-NAMINGCONVENTIONS-001`, `MCP-AUTH-042`
 62: - `^ISSUE-\d+$`: GitHub-backed canonical ID, e.g. `ISSUE-17`
 63: 
 64: The special create-only value `ISSUE-NEW` instructs the server to create a GitHub issue, rewrite the stored ID to `ISSUE-{number}`, and return the canonical form. After the first sync, the `description` / `body` of an `ISSUE-{number}` TODO is immutable from the server side; subsequent update calls surface the change as a GitHub issue comment instead of overwriting the body.
 65: 
 66: When populating `dependsOn`, each dependency ID must also conform to these patterns.
 67: 
 68: ## Querying TODOs
 69: 
 70: To retrieve a filtered list of TODOs:
 71: 
 72: ```yaml
 73: type: request
 74: payload:
 75:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-query-001
 76:   method: workflow.todo.query
 77:   params:
 78:     keyword: authentication
 79:     priority: high
 80:     section: Backend
 81:     done: false
 82: ```
 83: 
 84: All `params` fields are optional. Omit `params` entirely to return all TODOs. The response contains a paginated `items` array:
 85: 
 86: ```yaml
 87: type: result
 88: payload:
 89:   requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-query-001
 90:   result:
 91:     items:
 92:       - id: MCP-AUTH-001
 93:         title: Implement JWT authentication
 94:         section: Backend
 95:         priority: high
 96:         done: false
 97:         estimate: 4h
 98:         functionalRequirements: [FR-AUTH-001]
 99:         technicalRequirements: [TR-AUTH-001]
100:     totalCount: 1
101: ```
102: 
103: Valid `priority` values: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`.
104: 
105: ## Getting a Single TODO
106: 
107: To fetch the full detail of one TODO by ID:
108: 
109: ```yaml
110: type: request
111: payload:
112:   requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-get-001
113:   method: workflow.todo.get
114:   params:
115:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
116: ```
117: 
118: The result includes all fields: `implementationTasks`, `description`, `technicalDetails`, `remaining`, `doneSummary`, `dependsOn`, requirement arrays, and timestamps.
119: 
120: ## Selecting a TODO as Active Context
121: 
122: To set a TODO as the active working context for the session:
123: 
124: ```yaml
125: type: request
126: payload:
127:   requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-select-001
128:   method: workflow.todo.select
129:   params:
130:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
131: ```
132: 
133: Once selected, `workflow.todo.updateSelected` may be used to patch fields without repeating the ID on every call.
134: 
135: ## Creating a TODO
136: 
137: To create a new project task:
138: 
139: ```yaml
140: type: request
141: payload:
142:   requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-create-001
143:   method: workflow.todo.create
144:   params:
145:     id: MCP-AUTH-002
146:     title: Add rate limiting to auth endpoints
147:     section: Backend
148:     priority: medium
149:     estimate: 2h
150:     description:
151:       - Implement sliding window rate limiter
152:       - Configure 100 requests per 15 minutes
153:     implementationTasks:
154:       - task: Create RateLimitMiddleware
155:         done: false
156:       - task: Write unit tests
157:         done: false
158:     dependsOn: [MCP-AUTH-001]
159:     functionalRequirements: [FR-AUTH-002]
160:     technicalRequirements: [TR-AUTH-002]
161: ```
162: 
163: Required fields: `id`, `title`, `section`, `priority`. All other fields are optional.
164: 
165: To create a GitHub-backed TODO and let the server assign a canonical `ISSUE-{number}` ID:
166: 
167: ```yaml
168: type: request
169: payload:
170:   requestId: req-20260409T120004Z-create-issue-001
171:   method: workflow.todo.create
172:   params:
173:     id: ISSUE-NEW
174:     title: Capture sync regression in token refresh
175:     section: Issues
176:     priority: high
177: ```
178: 
179: The result `item.id` will contain the assigned `ISSUE-{number}` value.
180: 
181: ## Updating a TODO
182: 
183: To modify fields of an existing TODO:
184: 
185: ```yaml
186: type: request
187: payload:
188:   requestId: req-20260409T120005Z-update-001
189:   method: workflow.todo.update
190:   params:
191:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
192:     remaining: Integration tests still needed
193:     implementationTasks:
194:       - task: Create TokenService
195:         done: true
196:       - task: Create JwtValidator
197:         done: true
198:       - task: Add integration tests
199:         done: false
200: ```
201: 
202: Only include fields to change. To mark a TODO complete, set `done: true` and supply a `doneSummary`:
203: 
204: ```yaml
205: type: request
206: payload:
207:   requestId: req-20260409T120006Z-update-done-001
208:   method: workflow.todo.update
209:   params:
210:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
211:     done: true
212:     doneSummary: JWT authentication implemented and all tests passing
213: ```
214: 
215: To update the currently selected TODO without repeating the ID:
216: 
217: ```yaml
218: type: request
219: payload:
220:   requestId: req-20260409T120007Z-updatesel-001
221:   method: workflow.todo.updateSelected
222:   params:
223:     remaining: Need to add OpenAPI annotations
224: ```
225: 
226: ## Deleting a TODO
227: 
228: To remove a TODO permanently:
229: 
230: ```yaml
231: type: request
232: payload:
233:   requestId: req-20260409T120008Z-delete-001
234:   method: workflow.todo.delete
235:   params:
236:     id: MCP-AUTH-002
237: ```
238: 
239: ## Streaming Status Analysis
240: 
241: To request an AI-driven status analysis of a TODO, showing blockers and dependency state:
242: 
243: ```yaml
244: type: request
245: payload:
246:   requestId: req-20260409T120009Z-status-001
247:   method: workflow.todo.streamStatus
248:   params:
249:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
250: ```
251: 
252: The server emits a sequence of progress events followed by a completion event:
253: 
254: ```yaml
255: type: event
256: payload:
257:   event: workflow.todo.streamStatus
258:   data:
259:     eventType: status.progress
260:     sequence: 1
261:     timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:09Z
262:     message: Analyzing TODO dependencies...
263:     progress: 25
264: ---
265: type: event
266: payload:
267:   event: workflow.todo.streamStatus
268:   data:
269:     eventType: status.complete
270:     sequence: 4
271:     timestamp: 2026-04-09T12:00:12Z
272:     todoId: MCP-AUTH-001
273:     status: ready
274:     blockers: []
275:     dependencies: [MCP-AUTH-002]
276: ```
277: 
278: ## Streaming Plan Generation
279: 
280: To generate an implementation plan for a TODO and stream the result:
281: 
282: ```yaml
283: type: request
284: payload:
285:   requestId: req-20260409T120010Z-plan-001
286:   method: workflow.todo.streamPlan
287:   params:
288:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
289: ```
290: 
291: Events follow the same `eventType: plan.progress` / `eventType: plan.complete` pattern as status streaming. The completion event includes a structured plan document.
292: 
293: ## Streaming Implementation Execution
294: 
295: To execute an AI-driven implementation run for a TODO and stream progress:
296: 
297: ```yaml
298: type: request
299: payload:
300:   requestId: req-20260409T120011Z-implement-001
301:   method: workflow.todo.streamImplement
302:   params:
303:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
304: ```
305: 
306: Implementation events carry `eventType: implement.progress` and a final `eventType: implement.complete` with a results summary. Handle cancellation by sending a cancellation request; the stream emits a `eventType: status.cancelled` terminal event.
307: 
308: ## Analyzing Requirements for a TODO
309: 
310: To trigger requirements analysis and surface missing FR/TR traceability:
311: 
312: ```yaml
313: type: request
314: payload:
315:   requestId: req-20260409T120012Z-analyze-001
316:   method: workflow.todo.analyzeRequirements
317:   params:
318:     id: MCP-AUTH-001
319: ```
320: 
321: The result lists any detected requirement gaps and suggests FR/TR IDs to associate with the TODO.

330:   requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-create-001

333:   details:

335:     expectedFormat: "^[A-Z]+-[A-Z0-9]+-\\d{3}$"
336: ```

341: - `todo_already_exists`: a TODO with the same ID already exists
342: - `invalid_todo_id`: ID violates naming convention
343: - `no_selection`: `updateSelected` called with no active selection
344: - `stream_error`: a streaming operation failed mid-stream

Terminal request states never leave terminal.","- Each dispatch creates a durable attempt ID and random fence token before pool admission. Durable attempt states are \u0060Claimed\u0060, \u0060AdmissionPending\u0060, \u0060Running\u0060, \u0060Succeeded\u0060, \u0060Failed\u0060, \u0060Interrupted\u0060, \u0060Orphaned\u0060, or \u0060Cancelled\u0060. \u0060ReviewExecution\u0060 has a distinct execution ID, and the process-local AgentPool job ID is recorded as non-authoritative audit metadata when available.","- Claim is one atomic compare-and-swap over nonterminal request status, due time, lease expiry, attempt count, state version, and fence token. Renewal succeeds only for the current owner and fence. The attempt number is allocated durably before enqueue, so at most three pool admissions can be initiated for one request.","- The existing \u0060IAgentPoolService\u0060 remains backward-compatible and in-memory. Add only an internal process-singleton \u0060IHostileReviewDispatchCorrelation\u0060 with atomic \u0060TryReserve(attemptId)\u0060, \u0060AttachPoolJob(attemptId, poolJobId)\u0060, \u0060TryGet(attemptId)\u0060, and \u0060Remove(attemptId)\u0060; it is not a public API and is never treated as durable. The worker reserves before enqueue. Within one live process, retry or polling for an attempt sees either the reservation or attached job and never enqueues that attempt twice; an unresolved reservation is fenced and classified \u0060PoolAdmissionOutcomeUnknown\u0060, not blindly resubmitted.","- There is no exactly-once or durable pool-admission guarantee. Superseded FR/TR/TEST AC text and all evidence remain queryable as audit history but are not concurrently active acceptance criteria.","## Hostile-review worker contract","### Public schemas and operations","The only public operation names are \u0060hostile_review_submit\u0060, \u0060hostile_review_status\u0060, \u0060hostile_review_get\u0060, and \u0060hostile_review_query\u0060, with matching REST, typed-client, REPL, Director, and plugin-skill surfaces.","- Submit request fields: \u0060workspacePath\u0060 from authenticated context; \u0060targetType\u0060; \u0060mode\u0060; \u0060scopeStatement\u0060; \u0060artifactLinks[]\u0060 with type, locator, expected version/hash; \u0060requester\u0060 with agent, plugin/source, session ID, and turn ID when available; optional \u0060acceptanceCriteria[]\u0060. Reading status never changes any field.","- Get result fields: normalized request metadata, provenance, executions, findings, recommendations, verdict, request-quality assessment, and diagnostics. Unknown fields or malformed output fail the attempt.","### Ownership, defaults, and states","- A server-owned hosted worker is the only dispatcher. It reads the durable review queue, then calls the existing \u0060IAgentPoolService\u0060; the in-memory pool is an executor, not the queue authority.","- Configuration is \u0060HostileReviewWorkerOptions\u0060: enabled true; explicit agent name \u0060Astra\u0060; required model \u0060gpt-6-astra\u0060; required effort \u0060xhigh\u0060; maximum active queue 200, matching \u0060AgentPoolOptions.MaxQueueSize\u0060; maximum concurrent reviews 1; poll interval 2 seconds; lease duration 5 minutes; renewal interval 60 seconds; maximum attempts 3; retry delay 5 seconds with a 60-second cap; execution timeout 30 minutes; 64 links; 1 MiB per artifact; 8 MiB aggregate input; 2 MiB reviewer output; JSON depth 32. Invalid relationships such as renewal greater than or equal to lease fail startup validation.","- Effective model and effort are verified against the selected pool definition and returned execution metadata before a review can succeed. Missing or substituted model/effort is \u0060ModelUnavailable\u0060, not a silent fallback.","- Durable request states are \u0060Queued -\u003E Claimed -\u003E Running -\u003E Succeeded|Failed|Cancelled\u0060. A transient failure moves \u0060Claimed\u0060 or \u0060Running\u0060 to \u0060RetryWait\u0060, then back to \u0060Queued\u0060 when due. \u0060Cancelled\u0060 is reachable only from internal host/workspace lifecycle policy. Terminal request states never leave terminal.","- Each dispatch creates a durable attempt ID and random fence token before pool admission. Durable attempt states are \u0060Claimed\u0060, \u0060AdmissionPending\u0060, \u0060Running\u0060, \u0060Succeeded\u0060, \u0060Failed\u0060, \u0060Interrupted\u0060, \u0060Orphaned\u0060, or \u0060Cancelled\u0060. \u0060ReviewExecution\u0060 has a distinct execution ID, and the process-local AgentPool job ID is recorded as non-authoritative audit metadata when available.","- Claim is one atomic compare-and-swap over nonterminal request status, due time, lease expiry, attempt count, state version, and fence token. Renewal succeeds only for the current owner and fence. The attempt number is allocated durably before enqueue, so at most three pool admissions can be initiated for one request.","- The existing \u0060IAgentPoolService\u0060 remains backward-compatible and in-memory. Add only an internal process-singleton \u0060IHostileReviewDispatchCorrelation\u0060 with atomic \u0060TryReserve(attemptId)\u0060, \u0060AttachPoolJob(attemptId, poolJobId)\u0060, \u0060TryGet(attemptId)\u0060, and \u0060Remove(attemptId)\u0060; it is not a public API and is never treated as durable. The worker reserves before enqueue. Within one live process, retry or polling for an attempt sees either the reservation or attached job and never enqueues that attempt twice; an unresolved reservation is fenced and classified \u0060PoolAdmissionOutcomeUnknown\u0060, not blindly resubmitted.","- There is no exactly-once or durable pool-admission guarantee. A crash can occur after the model starts but before the pool job ID or result is durably observed. After process restart, an expired \u0060Claimed\u0060, \u0060AdmissionPending\u0060, or \u0060Running\u0060 attempt whose in-memory job cannot exist is durably closed as \u0060Orphaned\u0060 with \u0060PoolStateLostOnRestart\u0060; if the request is still eligible and below the attempt bound, a new attempt with a new fence is queued. This is bounded at-least-once model execution, so more than one model execution is possible.","- Completion acceptance requires request ID, attempt ID, fence token, unexpired ownership, and current state version. The first valid completion atomically creates the one accepted terminal result. Stale, orphaned, late, or duplicate outputs are discarded with sanitized diagnostics and cannot replace or add another accepted result, regardless of how many models executed.","- Graceful host shutdown stops new claims, internally calls \u0060CancelQueueItemAsync\u0060 for known live jobs, marks their attempts \u0060Interrupted\u0060, and moves eligible requests to \u0060RetryWait\u0060; abrupt process loss relies on lease expiry and the orphan rule. Workspace disable/delete may internally set \u0060CancelRequested\u0060, cancel a known running pool job, and terminate the request as \u0060Cancelled\u0060. No hostile-review public operation requests cancellation.","- When a pool job reaches terminal state or an attempt is interrupted, orphaned, timed out, or internally cancelled, the worker removes the process-local correlation and calls the existing internal \u0060RemoveQueueItemAsync\u0060 after processing has stopped. Disposal clears remaining correlations. These cleanup actions do not alter an already accepted terminal result.","- Transient classes are pool admission full, process-start transient, timeout, worker restart/orphan recovery, and explicitly classified model service unavailable. Malformed request/output, authorization failure, stale artifact, unsafe content, model/effort mismatch, and secret-policy failure are terminal. A transient failure after attempt 3 becomes \u0060Failed\u0060 with \u0060RetriesExhausted\u0060.","- No worker path exposes repair, apply, write, edit, TODO mutation, requirement mutation, or product-file mutation.","### Additional worker tests","\u0060HostileReviewWorker_StateMachine_QueuedClaimedRunningSucceeded\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_AdmissionRejected_RetryWaitThenRetry\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_LiveProcessRetry_ReusesCorrelatedPoolJob\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_AdmissionOutcomeUnknown_DoesNotReenqueueSameAttemptInProcess\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_Restart_ExpiredAttemptBecomesOrphanedAndNewAttemptIsBounded\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_CrashAfterAdmission_AllowsAtLeastOnceExecutionButOneAcceptedTerminalResult\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_LeaseLoss_StaleCompletionIsFenced\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_DuplicateCompletion_OneAcceptedTerminalResult\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_RetriesExhausted_FailsOnce\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_WorkspaceLifecycleCancellation_IsInternalAndFencesLateResult\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewStatus_ReadOnly_RejectsMutationFields\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_ProcessLifetimeCleanup_RemovesCorrelationAndTerminalPoolJob\u0060, \u0060HostileReviewWorker_ModelUnavailable_NoFallbackAndBoundedRetry\u0060, and \u0060HostileReviewWorker_InvalidOptions_FailStartup\u0060.","## Artifact authorization and protected execution","- Submit resolves identity only far enough to validate type, locator, caller access, workspace scope, and declared hash/version. Raw prompts and complete artifacts are not copied into results.","## Workspace hydration coordinator","### Durable receipt and transaction boundary","- Add \u0060WorkspaceImportReceipt\u0060 with receipt ID, source schema version, source root hash, source workspace key/path as immutable provenance, destination canonical workspace ID/path, state, state version, created/committed/activated UTC, activation stage, activation attempts, sanitized error code, and created-path manifest hash.","- Add \u0060WorkspaceImportEntityMap\u0060 with receipt ID, table name, source key, destination key, policy code, and provenance flag. PHASE 0: REQUIREMENTS GATE

Before production code, create these database-backed requirements with structured acceptanceCriteria through workflow.requirements.* operations.

FR-HANDOFF-001: Ingest workspace-scoped handoff documents from a contained file path, caller-supplied content, or MCP artifact reference.
Acceptance criteria: supports Markdown, text, JSON, and YAML inputs; rejects missing, unsupported, oversized, traversal, external, and reparse-escaping paths; maximum decoded input is 8 MiB.

FR-HANDOFF-002: Use the existing one-shot agent system to extract a structured MCP TODO draft.
Acceptance criteria: extraction uses a versioned prompt and strict JSON contract; malformed output produces diagnostics and never creates a TODO; unknown or missing source information is not silently discarded.

FR-HANDOFF-003: Validate and normalize generated TODO drafts.
Acceptance criteria: validate ID, title, section, priority, estimate, description, technical details, implementation tasks, dependencies, and requirement links; invalid or conflicting values produce field-specific diagnostics.

FR-HANDOFF-004: Support DraftOnly, RequireReview, and CreateWhenConfident modes.
Acceptance criteria: DraftOnly is the default and never mutates TODO state; RequireReview persists an approvable run without creating a TODO; CreateWhenConfident creates only when confidence is at least 0.75 and no error diagnostic exists.

FR-HANDOFF-005: Persist approved TODOs exclusively through the existing TODO service.
Acceptance criteria: successful creation produces exactly one TODO; replay of the same workspace, content hash, and prompt version returns the existing receipt; ID collisions require review and are never silently renamed.

FR-HANDOFF-006: Preserve auditable provenance and diagnostics for every run.
Acceptance criteria: retain run ID, source kind and locator, SHA-256 content hash, extraction time, prompt/template version, agent, model, confidence, mode, review state, diagnostics, and created TODO ID; raw credentials or source content are not copied into logs.

FR-HANDOFF-007: Provide behaviorally equivalent API, client, REPL, Director, MCP-tool, and plugin-skill entrypoints.
Acceptance criteria: every surface delegates to the same service, returns the same result contract, applies workspace isolation, and exposes ingest, inspect, and approval workflows.

201: ### Batch Create Or Update
 202: 
 203: When creating or updating multiple records, prefer the atomic batch commands instead of Markdown ingestion. Batch commands accept YAML `records:` arrays and fail all records if any record is invalid, conflicts, or is missing during update.

 205: Use per-kind commands when every record is the same type:

 217:         priority: high

 219:         title: Atomic validation

 525: 
 526: ## Error Handling
 527: 
 528: Common error codes:
 529: 
 530: - `requirement_not_found` - no requirement with the given ID
 531: - `requirement_already_exists` - ID already in use; update instead of create
 532: - `invalid_requirement_id` - ID does not match the expected regex for its type
 533: - `mapping_not_found` - mapping between the specified FR and TR does not exist
 534: - `invalid_mapping` - mapping references a non-existent FR, TR, or TEST ID
 535: - `document_generation_error` - failed to render the requested document format
 536: - `document_ingestion_error` - could not parse or persist the ingested document
 537: 
 538: ## Workflow Recommendations
 539: 
 540: When discovering or agreeing on new requirements during a session:
 541: 
 542: 1. Create the FR record immediately using `workflow.requirements.createFr`
 543: 2. Create the corresponding TR records using `workflow.requirements.createTr`
 544: 3. Create the TEST record using `workflow.requirements.createTest`
 545: 4. Link them with `workflow.requirements.createMapping`
 546: 5. Include the new IDs in the session log turn tags via `workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn`
 547: 
 548: Capture requirements as they emerge; do not defer to end of session. Requirements traceability is validated in CI and build failures result from missing mappings.

Routing shall support a global default target and per-workspace overrides. The feature shall include anti-loop protection (via \\u0060X-Mcp-Federation-Hop\\u0060 header with a configurable maximum hop count), transparent SSE/streaming forwarding for \\u0060/mcp-transport\\u0060, a runtime management REST API at \\u0060/mcpserver/federation\\u0060, and auto-discovery of federation targets from running tunnel providers.\\n\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Technical Implementation:** \\u0060FederationOptions\\u0060, \\u0060FederationRegistry\\u0060, \\u0060FederationProxyService\\u0060, \\u0060FederationMiddleware\\u0060, \\u0060FederationController\\u0060\\n\\n**Configuration:** \\u0060Mcp:Federation:Enabled\\u0060, \\u0060Mcp:Federation:Targets\\u0060, \\u0060Mcp:Federation:DefaultTarget\\u0060, \\u0060Mcp:Federation:WorkspaceRoutes\\u0060, \\u0060Mcp:Federation:MaxHops\\u0060\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"FR-MCP-078\",\"title\":\"GraphRAG Ad-Hoc Document Ingestion\",\"body\":\"The server shall accept raw text or markdown content via a REST endpoint and MCP tool, chunk it, generate embeddings, store it in the context database and vector index, and optionally trigger a GraphRAG re-index. Documents ingested this way shall use source type \\u0022adhoc-text\\u0022 by default and support caller-specified title, source type, and source key metadata.\\n\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060GraphRagController\\u0060 (\\u0060POST /mcpserver/graphrag/documents/ingest\\u0060), \\u0060McpServer.GraphRag\\u0060 (\\u0060GraphRagService\\u0060 ad-hoc ingestion path), \\u0060FwhMcpTools\\u0060 (graphrag ingest tool)\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"FR-MCP-079\",\"title\":\"GraphRAG Entity and Relationship CRUD\",\"body\":\"The server shall provide full CRUD operations for explicit graph entity nodes and relationship edges, persisted in workspace-scoped EF Core tables. Entities shall have name, type, description, and extensible JSON metadata. Relationships shall link two entities with a typed, weighted, described edge. Deleting an entity shall cascade to all its relationships. All operations shall be available via REST endpoints, MCP tools, and REPL commands.\\n\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060GraphRagController\\u0060 (entity \\u002B relationship endpoints), \\u0060McpServer.GraphRag\\u0060 (\\u0060GraphRagService\\u0060 entity / relationship CRUD), \\u0060GraphEntityEntity\\u0060, \\u0060GraphRelationshipEntity\\u0060, \\u0060FwhMcpTools\\u0060 (graphrag entity/relationship tools), \\u0060McpServer.Repl.Core\\u0060 (graphrag command shapes)\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"FR-MCP-080\",\"title\":\"GraphRAG Document Management\",\"body\":\"The server shall provide endpoints to list indexed documents with chunk counts and token totals, retrieve chunks for a specific document ordered by chunk index, and delete a document with cascade removal of its chunks and corresponding vector index entries. All operations shall be workspace-scoped and available via REST endpoints, MCP tools, and REPL commands.\\n\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060GraphRagController\\u0060 (document list/get/delete endpoints), \\u0060McpServer.GraphRag\\u0060 (\\u0060GraphRagService\\u0060 document management), \\u0060ContextDocumentEntity\\u0060, \\u0060ContextChunkEntity\\u0060, \\u0060FwhMcpTools\\u0060 (graphrag document tools)\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"FR-MCP-081\",\"title\":\"Byrd Iteration Phase and TODO Execution Persistence\",\"body\":\"The server shall persist Byrd iteration phases, decomposed execution TODOs, and TODO checkpoints so agents can resume multi-step work from MCP state instead of chat history. Terminal request states never leave terminal.","- Each dispatch creates a durable attempt ID and random fence token before pool admission. Durable attempt states are \u0060Claimed\u0060, \u0060AdmissionPending\u0060, \u0060Running\u0060, \u0060Succeeded\u0060, \u0060Failed\u0060, \u0060Interrupted\u0060, \u0060Orphaned\u0060, or \u0060Cancelled\u0060. \u0060ReviewExecution\u0060 has a distinct execution ID, and the process-local AgentPool job ID is recorded as non-authoritative audit metadata when available.","- Claim is one atomic compare-and-swap over nonterminal request status, due time, lease expiry, attempt count, state version, and fence token. Renewal succeeds only for the current owner and fence. The attempt number is allocated durably before enqueue, so at most three pool admissions can be initiated for one request.","- The existing \u0060IAgentPoolService\u0060 remains backward-compatible and in-memory. The worker reserves before enqueue. All dispatched calls are async (\\u0060Task\\u003CResult\\u003CT\\u003E\\u003E\\u0060).\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete - 37 unit tests passing\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060McpServer.Cqrs\\u0060 project\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"TR-MCP-CQRS-002\",\"title\":\"Decimal Correlation IDs\",\"body\":\"\\u0060CorrelationId\\u0060 uses format \\u0060{baseId}.{counter}\\u0060 where \\u0060baseId\\u0060 is a random 8-digit long (stable for the entire call tree) and \\u0060counter\\u0060 is a thread-safe (\\u0060Interlocked.Increment\\u0060) incrementing integer. Propagated via HTTP headers (\\u0060X-Correlation-Id\\u0060).\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060CorrelationId\\u0060\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"TR-MCP-CQRS-003\",\"title\":\"Dispatcher as ILoggerProvider with Context Registry\",\"body\":\"\\u0060Dispatcher\\u0060 implements \\u0060ILoggerProvider\\u0060 and maintains a \\u0060ConcurrentDictionary\\u003Clong, CallContext\\u003E\\u0060 of active contexts keyed by \\u0060CorrelationId.BaseId\\u0060. \\u0060DispatcherLogger\\u0060 (created by the provider) extracts correlation IDs from log scopes, looks up the \\u0060CallContext\\u0060, and enriches structured log entries with decomposed fields: \\u0060correlationId\\u0060, \\u0060correlationBaseId\\u0060, \\u0060correlationStep\\u0060, \\u0060operationName\\u0060, \\u0060userId\\u0060, \\u0060roles\\u0060, \\u0060elapsed\\u0060. \\u0060CallContext\\u0060 implements \\u0060ILogger\\u0060 and captures log entries to an internal list.\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060Dispatcher\\u0060, \\u0060DispatcherLogger\\u0060, \\u0060CallContext\\u0060\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"TR-MCP-CQRS-004\",\"title\":\"Automatic Result Monad Logging\",\"body\":\"After handler execution, the Dispatcher inspects the \\u0060Result\\u003CT\\u003E\\u0060: success results logged at \\u0060Debug\\u0060 level with elapsed time; failures with \\u0060Exception\\u0060 logged at \\u0060Error\\u0060 level with exception details; failures without exception logged at \\u0060Warning\\u0060 level. All logging includes decomposed correlation ID fields.\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060Dispatcher\\u0060\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"TR-MCP-CQRS-005\",\"title\":\"Pipeline Behaviors\",\"body\":\"\\u0060IPipelineBehavior\\u0060 wraps handler execution with pre/post processing. Terminal request states never leave terminal.","- Each dispatch creates a durable attempt ID and random fence token before pool admission. Durable attempt states are \u0060Claimed\u0060, \u0060AdmissionPending\u0060, \u0060Running\u0060, \u0060Succeeded\u0060, \u0060Failed\u0060, \u0060Interrupted\u0060, \u0060Orphaned\u0060, or \u0060Cancelled\u0060. \u0060ReviewExecution\u0060 has a distinct execution ID, and the process-local AgentPool job ID is recorded as non-authoritative audit metadata when available.","- Claim is one atomic compare-and-swap over nonterminal request status, due time, lease expiry, attempt count, state version, and fence token. Renewal succeeds only for the current owner and fence. The attempt number is allocated durably before enqueue, so at most three pool admissions can be initiated for one request.","- The existing \u0060IAgentPoolService\u0060 remains backward-compatible and in-memory. Add only an internal process-singleton \u0060IHostileReviewDispatchCorrelation\u0060 with atomic \u0060TryReserve(attemptId)\u0060, \u0060AttachPoolJob(attemptId, poolJobId)\u0060, \u0060TryGet(attemptId)\u0060, and \u0060Remove(attemptId)\u0060; it is not a public API and is never treated as durable. The worker reserves before enqueue. Within one live process, retry or polling for an attempt sees either the reservation or attached job and never enqueues that attempt twice; an unresolved reservation is fenced and classified \u0060PoolAdmissionOutcomeUnknown\u0060, not blindly resubmitted.","- There is no exactly-once or durable pool-admission guarantee. Templates are stored as YAML files, support Handlebars rendering with declared variables, and are filterable by category, tag, and keyword. A Director TUI tab shall enable template browsing and preview.\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060PromptTemplateController\\u0060, \\u0060PromptTemplateService\\u0060, \\u0060PromptTemplateRenderer\\u0060, \\u0060FwhMcpTools\\u0060 (6 template tools), \\u0060TemplateClient\\u0060. File Trust Bootstrap and Session Authenticity Validation\",\"body\":\"The server shall render a trust-bootstrap contract into \\u0060AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml\\u0060 that instructs agents to verify the marker signature, perform a nonce-based \\u0060/health\\u0060 challenge, and treat any signature or nonce mismatch as \\u0060MCP_UNTRUSTED\\u0060.\\n\\nWhen trust validation fails, the bootstrap flow shall stop using MCP services and shall not probe additional MCP endpoints. The marker contract shall remain explicit enough for \\u0060McpSession\\u0060, \\u0060McpTodo\\u0060, and \\u0060McpContext\\u0060 to follow the same verified bootstrap sequence without diverging on trust semantics.\\n\\n**Technical Implementation:** [TR-MCP-SEC-003](./Technical-Requirements.md#tr-mcp-sec-003) | [TR-MCP-AGENT-014](./Technical-Requirements.md#tr-mcp-agent-014) | [Mapping](./TR-per-FR-Mapping.md)\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060src/McpServer.Services/Services/MarkerFileService.cs\\u0060, \\u0060templates/prompt-templates.yaml\\u0060, \\u0060src/McpServer.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs\\u0060, \\u0060tools/powershell/McpSession.psm1\\u0060, \\u0060tools/powershell/McpTodo.psm1\\u0060, \\u0060tools/powershell/McpContext.psm1\\u0060, \\u0060docs/context/module-bootstrap.md\\u0060, \\u0060docs/USER-GUIDE.md\\u0060\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"FR-MCP-077\",\"title\":\"Server Federation and Request Proxying\",\"body\":\"The server shall support an opt-in federation mode that proxies incoming requests to a configured remote MCP server instance. Routing shall support a global default target and per-workspace overrides. The feature shall include anti-loop protection (via \\u0060X-Mcp-Federation-Hop\\u0060 header with a configurable maximum hop count), transparent SSE/streaming forwarding for \\u0060/mcp-transport\\u0060, a runtime management REST API at \\u0060/mcpserver/federation\\u0060, and auto-discovery of federation targets from running tunnel providers.\\n\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Technical Implementation:** \\u0060FederationOptions\\u0060, \\u0060FederationRegistry\\u0060, \\u0060FederationProxyService\\u0060, \\u0060FederationMiddleware\\u0060, \\u0060FederationController\\u0060\\n\\n**Configuration:** \\u0060Mcp:Federation:Enabled\\u0060, \\u0060Mcp:Federation:Targets\\u0060, \\u0060Mcp:Federation:DefaultTarget\\u0060, \\u0060Mcp:Federation:WorkspaceRoutes\\u0060, \\u0060Mcp:Federation:MaxHops\\u0060\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"FR-MCP-078\",\"title\":\"GraphRAG Ad-Hoc Document Ingestion\",\"body\":\"The server shall accept raw text or markdown content via a REST endpoint and MCP tool, chunk it, generate embeddings, store it in the context database and vector index, and optionally trigger a GraphRAG re-index. Documents ingested this way shall use source type \\u0022adhoc-text\\u0022 by default and support caller-specified title, source type, and source key metadata.\\n\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060GraphRagController\\u0060 (\\u0060POST /mcpserver/graphrag/documents/ingest\\u0060), \\u0060McpServer.GraphRag\\u0060 (\\u0060GraphRagService\\u0060 ad-hoc ingestion path), \\u0060FwhMcpTools\\u0060 (graphrag ingest tool)\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"FR-MCP-079\",\"title\":\"GraphRAG Entity and Relationship CRUD\",\"body\":\"The server shall provide full CRUD operations for explicit graph entity nodes and relationship edges, persisted in workspace-scoped EF Core tables. Entities shall have name, type, description, and extensible JSON metadata. Relationships shall link two entities with a typed, weighted, described edge. Deleting an entity shall cascade to all its relationships. All operations shall be available via REST endpoints, MCP tools, and REPL commands.\\n\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060GraphRagController\\u0060 (entity \\u002B relationship endpoints), \\u0060McpServer.GraphRag\\u0060 (\\u0060GraphRagService\\u0060 entity / relationship CRUD), \\u0060GraphEntityEntity\\u0060, \\u0060GraphRelationshipEntity\\u0060, \\u0060FwhMcpTools\\u0060 (graphrag entity/relationship tools), \\u0060McpServer.Repl.Core\\u0060 (graphrag command shapes)\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"FR-MCP-080\",\"title\":\"GraphRAG Document Management\",\"body\":\"The server shall provide endpoints to list indexed documents with chunk counts and token totals, retrieve chunks for a specific document ordered by chunk index, and delete a document with cascade removal of its chunks and corresponding vector index entries. All logging includes decomposed correlation ID fields.\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060Dispatcher\\u0060\",\"workspaceId\":\"F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\",\"priority\":\"medium\",\"status\":\"pending\",\"acceptanceCriteria\":[],\"scopeStartLayerKey\":\"layer-1\"},{\"id\":\"TR-MCP-CQRS-005\",\"title\":\"Pipeline Behaviors\",\"body\":\"\\u0060IPipelineBehavior\\u0060 wraps handler execution with pre/post processing. Acceptance Criteria: (AC1) acquiring the per-session lock for the same key blocks a second acquirer until release, while a different key acquires without blocking (KeyedAsyncLock); (AC2) DeleteTurnAsync continues to soft-delete a turn and refresh the parent turn count correctly under the lock.
